messages:
incbot: INCIDENT (P1) — multiple GPU containers in gpu-pool-3 unexpectedly restarting over the last 8m. Automatic alerts: memory allocation failures and GPU driver errors. Paging oncall.

samir: seeing it in the runtime logs: repeated allocations fail during prefill for long-context requests. Containers hit OOM-ish cudaAlloc failures then kube restarts. quick snippet:
```
2026-03-18T02:14:07Z ERROR cuda: cudaErrorMemoryAllocation at infer.cc:412
stack: cudnnCreateFail, kvcache_prefetch_alloc -> fallback-> SIGABRT
```

mona: traffic pattern: big spike from a single client sending huge context windows (30k tokens). Prefetch attempts tried to warm KV cache and pushed multiple containers above available vram.

laura_oncall: I'm on it. Taking lead. First actions: 1) add a temporary per-route max_context_tokens via route config (set to 8k) 2) disable aggressive KV prefetch for model-family redwood-13b-large on gpu-pool-3 3) cordon node gpu-node-7 and move new pods off it. Doing them now.

samir: +1. Also lowering batch size: set ENV MAX_BATCH_TOKENS=4096 on the deployment to stop further accumulation. Pushing a config patch to canary.

laura_oncall: deployed config patch to canary (deploy-bot confirmed). Rolling to pool-3 with 50% stagger. If restarts drop, we keep and then roll global.

deploy-bot: canary rollout successful on 2/2 pods. No restarts observed in the last 60s.

mona: early metrics: container restart count dropped from 47 -> 6 in first 3m after patch, error rate for streaming endpoints in EU-West dropped from 3.2% -> 0.9%. Customer traffic that used >12k contexts got 413/429 429 or 503 during the window.

customer-success: flagged impacted customers (enterprise accounts with large batch inference). Notifying top-10 impacted with incident note and mitigations. No data loss; only degraded/failed in-flight requests.

samir: root cause hypothesis: KV prefetch combined with long prompt tail and continuous batching pushes vram consumption past kernel allocator limits. Driver reports a fragmentation path leading to cudaMalloc failure (not classical OOM from a single big alloc). We should add a guard: refuse prefetch for requests that would enqueue >X prefetched tokens across the batch.

laura_oncall: agreed. Immediate triage checklist:
- Isolate noisy client IPs and throttle (mona + network team)
- Keep the canary config for 30m and monitor restarts
- Schedule a short capacity bump for gpu-pool-3 if restarts persist (ops infra)
- Postmortem owner: nate (assigned)

nate: taking postmortem. I'll capture timelines, config diffs, and a plan: 1) implement prefetch budget enforcement 2) add kernel-level fallback to coldmodel with warnings 3) improve our circuit-breaker for long-context routes so they hit 429 earlier rather than trigger allocator failure.

samir: created quick PR for prefetch_budget_guard and a canary rule: if total_prefetch_tokens_in_batch > 65536 then skip prefetch and mark route as "reduced-prefetch". PR: https://git.internal/r/infra/1234

laura_oncall: monitoring window 15m left. If no further restarts, we'll declare mitigation successful and close paging but keep incident channel open for full postmortem.

mona: note for postmortem: client patterns that send many small messages concatenated into one long context cause surprising prefetch multipliers. We should add a usage recommendation and suggest server-side trimming + metrics to identify such call patterns.

customer-success: update sent to impacted customers, offering credits for degraded ops. They're asking for ETA on permanent fix — we'll provide postmortem ETA in 48h.

laura_oncall: handing off monitoring to nate for the overnight rotation. I remain available if things regress. Marking first-responder -> laura_oncall, next-responder -> nate.

incbot: Incident status: mitigation applied, oncall handed off. Follow-up: postmortem assigned.
